fullPassage: Volunteering has a great deal of benefits. Not only do you make a positive impact on someone's life, but you gain valuable skills for your career. It even reduces stress and anxiety. With busy schedules, it can be hard to find the time to commit to volunteer work. These days, however, you can make a huge difference in the lives of others from your own home by virtually volunteering. First, you could be a part of the effort to lend support to senior citizens who struggle with loneliness. Typically, volunteer "phone friends" make regular calls to chat and check in with these people. Second, you can help people with low or no vision with their everyday tasks. Through a live video call, you can offer visual assistance to those who need it.

questions.passage: I have a bad case of anxiety that <u>ⓐ comes</u> from not checking my phone. I spend most of my day on social media. I fear <u>ⓑ missing</u> out on social media. My mom thinks I'm <u>ⓒ addicting</u> to my phone. Older people think teenagers like me have an addiction to their phones and computers. But I wouldn't say it's an addiction to a device. It's an addiction to <u>ⓓ being</u> online, or in other words, a fear of not being online. Basically, I have severe FOMO, for <u>ⓔ which</u> I'm in desperate need of a cure.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.korean: 엄마는 내가 핸드폰에 중독되었다고 생각한다. be addicted to ~는 '~에 중독되다'라는 수동 표현입니다. 주어 I가 중독의 대상이므로 과거분사 addicted가 와야 합니다.
det.analysis: 원문: My mom thinks I'm addicted to my phone.
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: While walking in the park, I probably glanced at my phone 20 times. At one moment, I looked at the people around me, most of (A) [whom / who] had their eyes glued to their phones. I moved my gaze upward and noticed how purely blue the sky was, without a single cloud in sight. After lunch, I took out my old guitar from under my bed. At first, it was because I was bored, but I ended up (B) [playing / to play] it all afternoon. It just felt great that I was lost in (C) [doing / to do] something for several hours without getting interrupted by my phone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그들 대부분은 눈을 핸드폰에 붙이고 있었다. (A) 전치사 of 뒤 → 목적격 whom. (B) end up + v-ing = 결국 ~하게 되다. (C) be lost in + v-ing = ~에 빠져 있다(전치사 in 뒤 동명사).
det.analysis: 원문: most of whom had their eyes glued to their phones
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

det.korean: 오래된 습관은 쉽게 사라지지 않는다. 영어 속담으로, 오래된 습관은 바꾸기 어렵다는 의미.
det.analysis: 원문: Old habits die hard.
det.tip: 서술형 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: After lunch, I took out my old guitar from under my bed. At first, it was because I was bored, but I ended up playing it all afternoon. It didn't matter that I'm not really good at it. It just felt great that I was lost in (do) __________ something for several hours without getting interrupted by my phone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰시오.

det.korean: 나는 무언가를 하는 데 빠져 있었다. 전치사 in 뒤 동명사(v-ing) 필요. be lost in + v-ing = ~에 빠져 있다.
det.analysis: 원문: I was lost in doing something
det.tip: 서술형 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.
